documents.title: Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Intimation
Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM

analysis.summary: Bhansali Engineering Polymers Limited reported a 53.3% YoY increase in revenue from operations to ₹472.2 crores for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA rising 44.5% to ₹92.3 crores. The company is executing a capex of approximately ₹200 crore to expand its capacity from 75,000 MTPA to 100,000 MTPA, with commissioning targeted by 30 September, 2026. Management expects optimal utilisation of this expanded capacity by the end of FY28, supported by robust domestic demand in the automotive and consumer durables sectors. Bhansali Engineering Polymers Limited reported a revenue decrease of 8.7% for FY26 to INR 1,276.0 crores, while EBITDA grew by 1.3% to INR 255.2 crores and PAT rose by 0.1% to INR 180.2 crores. Management highlighted an ongoing capacity expansion from 75,000 MTPA to 100,000 MTPA with a commissioning target of September 2026, backed by a ₹200 crore capex funded entirely through internal accruals.

guidance.claim: The company expects optimal utilisation of its expanded capacity by the end of FY28.
guidance.quote: Optimal utilisation of expanded capacity expected by end of FY28.

guidance.claim: Optimal utilisation of expanded capacity is expected by the end of FY28.
guidance.quote: • Optimal utilisation of expanded capacity expected by end of FY28.

demand_outlook.claim: Domestic demand for ABS is expected to be driven by robust growth in end-user industries such as consumer durables and automotive.
demand_outlook.quote: Robust growth in end-user industries like consumer durables (air conditioners, refrigerators) and automotive will drive the domestic demand for ABS.

demand_outlook.claim: The global market is shifting toward specialty and colored grades, moving away from commoditized transparent resins to higher-margin applications.
demand_outlook.quote: The global market is shifting toward specialty & colored grades, moving away from commoditized transparent resins to higher-margin applications.

demand_outlook.claim: Consumption is being accelerated by electric vehicle adoption as manufacturers prioritize lightweight, high-performance plastics for interior trims and battery housings.
demand_outlook.quote: EV (Electric Vehicle) adoption is accelerating consumption as manufacturers prioritize lightweight, high-performance plastics for interior trims and battery housings.

demand_outlook.claim: The consumption of ABS in India exceeds domestic manufacturing output, providing growth potential.
demand_outlook.quote: There is immense scope for growth, considering the existing supply and demand mismatch, and knowing the fact that the consumption of ABS in India is voluminously larger as compared to the combined output of the domestic manufacturers.

demand_outlook.claim: India's major home appliances market was estimated at Rs 1.86 lakh crore in 2025 and is projected to experience steady growth.
demand_outlook.quote: The major home appliances market in India was estimated at approximately `1.86 lakh crore in 2025 and is projected to grow steadily over the coming years, supported by increasing household penetration, replacement demand and the expansion of organised retail and e-commerce channels.

capex_expansion.claim: Capacity expansion from 75,000 TPA to 100,000 TPA is progressing with critical equipment orders placed.
capex_expansion.quote: The implementation of capacity expansion from existing 75000 TPA to 1,00,000 TPA is progressing well and orders have been placed for critical long delivery equipments.

capex_expansion.claim: Commissioning of the expanded ABS capacity is expected by the end of September 2026.
capex_expansion.quote: The balance engineering, procurement and construction work is in progress and the commissioning of enhanced capacity is expected to be completed by end of September, 2026.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA increased by 44.5% YoY in Q1 FY27 to ₹92.3 crores, with margins at 19.2% compared to 20.0% in Q1 FY26.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA increased by 44.5% YoY in Q1 FY27 to ₹ 92.3 crores, from ₹ 63.9 crores in Q1 FY26, with margins at 19.2% for Q1 FY27 as compared to 20.0% in Q1 FY26.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA increased by 33.1% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR 74.3 crores, with margins at 21.8%.
margins_costs.quote: • EBITDA increased by 33.1% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR 74.3 crores, with margins at 21.8%; for FY26, EBITDA grew by 1.3% to INR 255.2 crores, with margins at 20.0%.

margins_costs.claim: Operating margin reached 19.42% in FY 2025-26 compared to 17.43% in FY 2024-25, while net profit margin was 14.14%.
margins_costs.quote: The operating margin for FY 2025-26 was 19.42 % as compared to 17.43 % for FY 2024-25, whereas the net profit margin stood at 14.14 % as compared to 12.86 % for the previous FY.

orders_capacity.claim: Production volume reached 71,601.50 TPA against an installed capacity of 75,000 TPA in FY 2025-26.
orders_capacity.quote: During FY 2025-26, the Company achieved production volume of 71601 TPA against installed capacity of 75,000 TPA.

orders_capacity.claim: Sales volume for FY 2025-26 was 71,501 TPA compared to 74,381 TPA in the prior year.
orders_capacity.quote: Sales volume stood at 71501 TPA (Previous year - 74381 TPA).

capital_allocation.claim: A healthy dividend payout of approximately 50%+ reflects disciplined capital allocation and shareholder returns.
capital_allocation.quote: Healthy dividend payout (~50%+)* reflects disciplined capital allocation and shareholder returns.

capital_allocation.claim: Consistent positive operating cash flows support self-funded growth without relying on external capital.
capital_allocation.quote: Consistent positive operating cash flows (CFO) support self-funded growth without reliance on external capital.

capital_allocation.claim: A debt-free balance sheet ensures zero financial risk and high resilience.
capital_allocation.quote: Debt-free balance sheet ensures zero financial risk and high resilience.

capital_allocation.claim: The company has a debt-free balance sheet with a gross debt to equity ratio of 0.0x.
The Board declared three interim dividends of Re. 1 each and recommended a final dividend of Re. 1 per equity share for FY 2025-26.
capital_allocation.quote: Continuing with the practice of rewarding shareholders, the Board declared three Interim Dividends, each of Re.1/- (collectively 300%) per Equity shares of Re.1/- and recommended a Final Dividend of Re.1/- (100 %) per Equity Share for the Financial Year Ended 31st March, 2026.

capital_allocation.claim: The company maintains its status as a zero-debt company.
capital_allocation.quote: The Company continues to enjoy the status of a “Zero Debt Company”.

capital_allocation.claim: Business operations will be sustained through internal accruals with no changes in financing structure.
capital_allocation.quote: There was no change in financing pattern and the Company would be able to sustain its business operations through internal accruals.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company maintains a strong liquidity position to provide a cushion against cyclicality and working capital shocks.
risks_headwinds.quote: Strong liquidity position, providing a cushion against cyclicality and working capital shocks.

risks_headwinds.claim: The domestic ABS industry faces foreign exchange risk as key monomers Styrene and Acrylonitrile rely on imports.
risks_headwinds.quote: The ABS business in India is exposed to the risk of foreign exchange fluctuations, as the key raw materials viz. ‘Styrene’ and ‘Acrylonitrile’ are import dependent, as there is no indigenous producer for these monomers.

risks_headwinds.claim: Domestic producers deliberate to keep low raw material inventories to mitigate international price fluctuation risks.
risks_headwinds.quote: The limitation arises out of deliberate decision on the part of domestic manufacturers to keep low inventories of its imported key raw materials which is more than 85% (i.e. Styrene and Acrylonitrile monomers) to limit the risk of price fluctuations which may result in huge loss, if the price of monomers drastically falls in the international market, which happen many a times due to unpredictable reasons, i.e. fluctuation in price of crude oil, benzene and ethylene.
